metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent failed to create the unseen_movies sheet (reward 0.0, 33 turns). The agent reliably navigated to https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/ in Chrome (steps 3-6) and scrolled through the IMDB Top 250 page.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome browser to specific URLs, demonstrated at steps 3-6. Can interact with Chrome UI for browser management actions.
metadata.failure_analysis: Agent failed after step 16 when switching back to LibreOffice Calc. The browser navigation to IMDB Top 250 was completed reliably.
metadata.task_rationale: Extended the browser navigation sub-goal (steps 3-6 reliable prefix) with a bookmarking action. Both navigation and bookmarking are within the demonstrated Chrome interaction capability. Checks all bookmark folders (not just bookmark bar) to allow flexibility.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to the IMDB Top 250 page and bookmarking it. The custom metric iteratively searches all Chrome bookmark folders for any URL containing 'imdb.com/chart/top'. Negative control fails because initial state has no IMDB chart bookmark. [Fixed: replaced nested def _search_bookmarks with an inline iterative stack-based search to eliminate any nested def statement that the validator flags as a non-conforming metric function name]
fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed nested helper function 'search_bookmarks' to '_search_bookmarks' in metrics/chrome.py to satisfy rule-based validation requiring all non-private function definitions in metric files to follow check_{semantic}__{32-char-md5} naming convention.

Fix 2: Replaced nested 'def _search_bookmarks' with an inline iterative stack-based search inside check_imdb_top250_bookmarked__27137be4f649298821e5e5376fdad889, eliminating the nested def entirely so the validator no longer flags it as a non-conforming function name.

validation.fix_applied: Replaced nested 'def _search_bookmarks' with an inline iterative stack-based search inside the metric function, eliminating all nested def statements so the validator no longer flags any non-conforming function name
llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_bookmarks) correctly reads Chrome's Bookmarks JSON file from disk, returning all bookmark roots — file-based access requires no postconfig or dialog reopening.

Metric correctly handles the expected parameter: since expected.type='rule', the framework returns the rules dict directly, and the metric uses expected.get('expected_url_fragment', ...) which is the correct access pattern.
URL fragment 'imdb.com/chart/top' correctly matches the IMDB Top 250 chart URL (https://www.imdb.com/chart/top).
Iterative stack-based search covers all bookmark folders (bookmark_bar, other, synced) and nested subfolders, providing full coverage without limiting to a single location.
Instruction coverage is complete: verifying that a bookmark with the chart URL exists implicitly confirms both navigation to the page and bookmarking it.
Negative control resistance is sound: initial state has IMDB homepage open (not the chart page), and no IMDB chart bookmark exists, so the evaluator correctly fails the do-nothing state.
Edge cases handled: result=None returns 0.0, and the iterative search handles arbitrary nesting of dicts and lists.
